note: Autonomous driving (Alphabet company, Mountain View). Waymo's own post of 2026-02-02: a $16B investment round at $126B post-money, led by Dragoneer, DST Global and Sequoia, with GV named among the investors. The firm's own post the same day (https://www.gv.com/news/waymo-gv) calls it GV 'officially starting a new ride, participating in Waymo's latest funding round', so this is the entry: a late-stage round after Waymo's 2020, 2021 and 2024 raises, read Growth. Private at that mark (decisions D4); aligned with a16z and Sequoia ($126B, 2026-02).

funding_rounds.lead: Dragoneer Investment Group, DST Global, Sequoia Capital

note: AI estate-planning platform for wealth advisors (offices in Tempe and New York; the 2022 seed release and the Series B dateline place it in the Phoenix area). Seed $16M led by Anthos Capital (2022-03-22, no GV). GV led the $30M Series A on 2024-09-16 (the company's own post), matching the firm's /ai list ('Invested' 2024-09). GV followed in the $65M Series B of 2026-04-16 led by Titanium Ventures, Pruven Capital, The K Fund and Dynasty. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News + the company's newsroom): the Series B disclosed no valuation and no $1B+ priced round was found, so below_1b.

funding_rounds.lead: Titanium Ventures, Pruven Capital, The K Fund, Dynasty Financial Partners

note: Kubernetes/GitOps tooling (Flux). Accel led the $5M Series A (TechCrunch 2014-12-03; GV not named). GV led the $15M Series B (TechCrunch 2016-05-11: 'GV had not invested before'; Accel followed), so the entry is Growth. Weaveworks announced on 2024-02-05 that it was shutting down commercial operations after an acquisition fell through (TechCrunch), hence defunct; the Flux project lives on at the CNCF. Sibling Accel still reads private: the shutdown is fresher cited evidence. London HQ: the Series A coverage has the money expanding a US organization 'to complement its team in London'; aligned with Accel.

Research-collaboration cloud software for pharma R&D (Cambridge MA). TechCrunch 2011-07-07: 'Google Ventures has quietly invested in a stealth startup called Wingu', no amount or round named; no other source read names the round, so the stage is undetermined. Acquired by PerkinElmer in 2014 (the firm's own exit line, 'Acquired by PerkinElmer, 2014').

Marc Lore's food halls and delivery company (Wonder Group, New York). Stage disputes the Form D band: the band read Wonder Group, Inc.'s first Form Ds (filed from 2024, rounds of $100M to $1.66B) as a Growth entry, but the firm's own post by Dave Munichiello, the GV partner on the row, says 'Founders whom I've backed at the Series A include ... Marc Lore (Wonder)'. Entry dated 2020 from Wonder's 2023 tender-offer filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995164/000110465923109094/tm2328273d1_ex99-a1a.htm): 'Mr. Munichiello has served as a director of Wonder since 2020'; the Series A's own amount and month are not on record. GV was an existing investor in the May 2025 $600M round (with NEA, Accel, Forerunner) and the July 2026 $650M Series D at a $9B pre-money valuation (Restaurant Dive, 2026-07-16). Mark aligned with BCV and General Catalyst ($9B, 2026-07-16); Accel's below_1b carries no mark.

funding_rounds.lead: New Enterprise Associates, Accel, Google Ventures, Forerunner

note: Educational coding robots Dash and Dot (Play-i, renamed Wonder Workshop; Silicon Valley, San Mateo). Robohub 2013-10-29: Play-i came out of stealth 'after receiving a $1million seed fund round from investors like Google Ventures', so the entry is that 2013 seed. Graduated: the company later raised a named Series B, $20M co-led by WI Harper and Idea Bulb (ZDNet 2016-07-28), after a $6.9M 2015 round (WI Harper, Madrona, CRV), and a $41M round led by Tencent in 2017. Acquired: the Wonder Workshop brand and its Dash robots now sell under 'MORAVIA Education, Inc' of Celebration, Florida (makewonder.com, read 2026-09-28); the acquisition date and price were not found, so the note keeps the successor only. City is the company's own last HQ, San Mateo.

funding_rounds.lead: WI Harper Group, Idea Bulb Ventures

note: Personalised children's books (Lost My Name, renamed Wonderbly; London). The Guardian 2015-06-25: the London firm's $9M round was 'led by Google Ventures with ... Greycroft and The Chernin Group'; Wikipedia names it the Series A. Earlier money was small angel funding and a Dragons' Den deal, without GV. Ravensburger led an $8.5M Series B in July 2017. Graphite Capital bought the company in July 2021 (the firm's own exit line) and Penguin Random House acquired it in June 2025 (Wikipedia).

MicroOrganoSphere precision-oncology platform (Duke spin-out, Durham NC). Duke's release 2021-07-08: a $70M Series A led by Mubadala Capital, 'joined by new investors GV (formerly Google Ventures)', LSP, Catalio and others; Felicis, Two Sigma and Pear were existing investors. The Series A was extended to over $89M in July 2022; a $19.4M Form D followed in 2025. The 2022 Form D names Wesley Chan, Felicis's partner, not a GV seat. Entry date from the round's own release, not the Form D anchor.

Hybrid-cloud data warehouse (Mountain View). SiliconANGLE 2018-07-31, at the stealth exit with $44M: 'Draper Fisher Jurvetson, Google Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung Ventures and Third Point Ventures all participating in the Series A'. Menlo dates its own Series A entry to 2015, so the round may have closed in parts before its announcement; the entry date is the announcement's (medium confidence). Next47 led the $48M Series B (October 2018); DFJ Growth led the $81M Series C with GV as an existing investor (June 2019); a $75M Series C1 followed in November 2021. No priced round at $1B+ found; aligned with Menlo and IVP (private, below_1b, Mountain View).

Email tracking and sales engagement (Boston). The prefilled Seed is borne out by TechCrunch 2011-09-27: $1M 'from Google Ventures, Foundry Group and other investors'. Graduated: IDG Ventures led a named $4M Series A with 'seed investors Google Ventures, Foundry Group' (TechCrunch 2012-06-20; the article also has the company moving from Cambridge to Boston); the Form D layer agrees (a $14.7M raise in 2013). Acquired by Vendasta (the firm's own exit line; Battery's row dates it 2022); aligned with Battery on status and city.

Conversion and on-site marketing software (London). TechCrunch 2015-06-25: the London company's $11.5M Series A came from SoftBank Capital and Google Ventures, Avid Larizadeh Duggan leading GV's side; the earlier ~$1.2M (Hoxton Ventures, Robin Klein) did not include GV. A further $6M followed in May 2017. Acquired by Publicis Groupe in 2023 (the firm's own exit line).

Mobile ad formats and attention analytics (New York, per Wikipedia). Still private: Abu Dhabi's Multiply (an IHC subsidiary) bought a stake in September 2020 to finance growth, which Campaign Middle East reports as an investment alongside Google Ventures and Union Square Ventures, not a takeover; no exit line on the firm's list. No priced round at $1B+ on record. Aligned with USV (private, below_1b, New York).

Bored Ape Yacht Club studio (Miami). The only priced round on record is the $450M seed at $4B led by Andreessen Horowitz (TechCrunch 2022-03-22), whose investor list (Animoca, LionTree, Sound Ventures, Thrive, FTX, MoonPay) does not name GV; the firm has listed Yuga since 2022 (David Krane, Tom Hulme) but no post, filing or press item read names the round GV bought, so the stage is undetermined. Mark aligned with a16z and Lightspeed ($4B, 2022-03), stale; Lightspeed's row notes a reported 2026 secondary near half that, still above $1B and not a primary mark.

Specialty-medication prescribing platform (Boston). SR One led the $5.6M Series A with Atlas (TechCrunch 2015-04-02, GV not named); 'GV (formerly Google Ventures) and ... SR One were also in' the $25M Series B led by Qiming US (TechCrunch 2017-04-20), matching the firm's first listing in 2017, so the entry is Growth. Acquired by Allscripts in 2019 (Wikipedia's Allscripts/Veradigm history; the firm's exit line).

Cloud video-encoding API and the VideoJS player (Y Combinator, San Francisco). TechCrunch 2012-07-26: Brightcove paid $30M for Zencoder, which had 'raised just $2 million, mostly through a Series A round raised in April 2011'. No source read names GV in that or any round (Google News and TechCrunch's own search), so the stage is undetermined; the firm lists it as exited ('Acquired by Brightcove, 2012'). The 2024-26 AI coding company named Zencoder is unrelated. Aligned with a16z and YC.

Life-sciences data and insights platform. Anju Software's release of 2018-10-02 (linked from the firm's own listing) announces the acquisition of 'San Francisco-based Zephyr Health', 'venture backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, Icon Ventures, and Google Ventures'. The $15M round of January 2014 was co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Jafco without naming GV (TechCrunch); the firm first lists the company in 2015 (Blake Byers), and no source read names the round GV joined, so undetermined.

Gifting checkout and storefront software for e-commerce brands (zest.co), founded 2022 by Alex Ingram and Jeremy Feinstein, ex-Flatiron Health. TechCrunch 2022-11-15: '$4 million in seed funding led by GV' with BoxGroup, Character, Operator Partners, Bungalow and Company Ventures. Country and city from the company's own privacy policy (an East 49th Street, New York NY 10017 address; Manhattan venue in its terms), so the Wikidata GB was a one-word join to another Zest and is disputed. No later round found. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

RAS-pathway oncology company spun out of BridgeBio Pharma (South San Francisco, per its S-1). The S-1's related-party section: the Series A preferred (2023 to April 2024, $79.2M) went only to a BridgeBio Pharma subsidiary, and the Series B preferred ($200M, April to May 2024) went to outside investors. BridgeBio Pharma's release of 2024-05-02 names GV among the participants in that $200M financing (led by Cormorant, co-led by Omega), so GV entered at the Series B: Growth. Listed through the August 2025 merger with Helix Acquisition Corp. II; GV 2023, L.P. holds 2,823,126 shares in the S-1's selling holder table. Value is the market cap, $305.46M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the 2025 float as the canonical figure; the band is unchanged.

Commercial drone operating system and analytics (Y Combinator W13, San Francisco). TechCrunch 2013-05-15: the $10.7M Series A 'is led by Andreessen Horowitz, and backed by Google Ventures', after a small seed that does not name GV. Kleiner led a $25M round in 2014 and Next World Capital a $30M Series C in 2016. Airware shut in September 2018; Delair bought its Redbird analytics software and IP and took 26 staff while the hardware went to auction (TechCrunch 2018-10-29), so the prefilled acquired stands (a16z and Felicis read acquired; First Round and YC read defunct).

Apple-harvesting robots (SRI International spin-out). TechCrunch 2017-05-03: 'GV ... is leading a $10 million investment', the Series A, after $2M of seed funding (SRI Ventures spin-out, GV not named). The Hayward company closed in summer 2021; Wavemaker Labs bought its IP in October 2021 and revived it under new leadership (TechCrunch 2022-02-02), so the row reads acquired out of the shutdown, with Wavemaker as successor.

Back-office-as-a-service for startups and small businesses. TechCrunch 2013-07-11: the $7M Series A was co-led by Sherpa Ventures and e.ventures 'and includes Google Ventures', the existing seed investors being CrunchFund and Mark Pincus (the $1.5M seed of November 2012 names no GV). Status aligned with Headline's row: merged in 2016 with the founder's Scalus into HireAthena.

Amino Apps (Narvii), mobile interest communities, New York. USV's own post of 2014-07-08 announces its Series A investment with co-investors 'Google Ventures, SV Angel, Box Group, Kal Vepuri and Slow Ventures'; Wikipedia calls the same 2014 money a $1.65M seed 'primarily from Union Ventures' with Google Ventures, so the label rests on the lead's own contemporaneous word (medium). MediaLab bought the app (January 2020 per USV's row, January 2021 per Wikipedia) and the platform stopped in December 2025: acquired, aligned with USV. First Round's 'Amino' is Amino Payments of Philadelphia, a different company.

Bitcoin exchange (Y Combinator S13). TechCrunch 2015-04-06: 'Google Ventures participated in the seed round through Kevin Rose and Chris Hutchins'; TechCrunch 2013-09-18 dates that seed (about $1M before Centralway's $250k on the same terms, total ~$1.6M) to 2013. Shut its service on 2015-04-10 after failing to raise more (TechCrunch 2015-04-06): defunct. City aligned with YC's directory row (New York). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

On-demand private rooms and flexible workspace, 'based in Montreal, Canada' (Wikipedia), confirming the Wikidata country. Rounds read: $6M Series A led by RRE (2014), $20M Series B from Valar (2015), $40M Series C led by Menlo (December 2016); none names GV, which the firm first lists in 2017, and the $122.5M raised by June 2018 implies a later round not found, so undetermined. Industrious acquired key assets of Breather's platform in May 2021 (Wikipedia): acquired.

The YouTube founders' internet company (Delicious, Zeen, MixBit). TechCrunch 2014-06-06: AVOS sold Delicious and turned from an incubator into a single company working on MixBit, with offices in San Mateo and New Zealand. MixBit ceased operations on 2018-08-21 (Wikipedia's MixBit article), so defunct. A Series A closed in April 2012 (FinSMEs headline) but no source read names GV in it, so the stage is undetermined.

Agent, the context-aware Android app on the firm's 2014-19 archived list, was Tagstand's product: TechCrunch 2019-03-15 says Kulveer Taggar's Y Combinator-backed 'NFC-triggered task launcher Tagstand ... pivoted into app settings configurer Agent, which pivoted into automatic location sharing app Status', before he co-founded Zeus Living in 2016. No source read names GV's round or gives the company's own end (shutdown or sale), so status is unknown and the stage undetermined.

iOS-to-Android cross-compiler (Y Combinator W11, San Francisco). TechCrunch 2014-02-05: in July 2013 Apportable raised $2.4M 'from Initialized Capital and Google Ventures, among others', then $5M from Initialized, Danhua Capital and Y Combinator. Neither round is named in any source read, so the stage is undetermined, dated by the July 2013 round. Status aligned with YC's directory (acquired); no sale document was read.

Hosted mobile sites plus Google mobile ads for local businesses (founder Steve Espinosa; 'Google's biggest reseller of mobile ads'). TechCrunch 2012-03-27: a '$1.5 million seed round' with Google Ventures and Eric Schmidt's Tomorrow Ventures involved. No source read gives its fate (the appstack.com domain is now for sale) or its city, so status unknown and city_unknown. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Social learning games for children, founded 2011 by Thiel Fellow Andrew Hsu (StartX). TechCrunch 2011-08-03: '$1.5 million in seed funding from Google Ventures, Foundation Capital and Playdom founder Rick Thompson'. TechCrunch 2012-02-11 reported deep staff cuts; no source read gives the company's end or its city, so status unknown and city_unknown. Cherry's 'Airy' (Berlin messaging platform) is a different company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Community-platform startup co-founded by Lady Gaga's manager Troy Carter (Little Monsters). TechCrunch 2012-02-16: Backplane 'raised an early ... seed round' of $1.8M from investors 'including Google Ventures, Founders Fund Angel, Menlo Ventures, SV Angel, i/o Ventures, and Tomorrow Ventures', and the same day closed a named Series A of $4-5M (Sequoia, Greylock Discovery, Battery, Formation 8), so the seed graduated. Entry dated by TechCrunch 2012-01-20, the first piece naming Google Ventures in the round. In April 2016 Backplane ran out of money and sold its assets to a group of previous and new investors who meant to restart it (TechCrunch 2016-04-11): acquired out of insolvency.

funding_rounds.round: Asset sale to previous and new investors

note: Mobile marketing automation (push, in-app messaging), later Carnival.io. The prefilled public/$25.1B is Carnival Corporation's float joined on the name (cik_weak) and is disputed: Global Venturing: 'The company, then known as Carnival Labs, raised $2.4m in 2013 from GV, then called Google Ventures, Lerer Ventures, Flybridge ...', and GV exited when Sailthru bought the 'US-based' company (MediaPost, 2016-04-07; terms undisclosed). TechCrunch 2014-01-10 has the round led by Gary Vaynerchuk and Lerer Ventures and the company 'based in New York and New Zealand'. The round is not named, so the stage is undetermined.

Private group photo-sharing app (Cluster Labs: Brenden Mulligan, Taylor Hughes, Riz Sattar). The prefilled public/$4,399 is another registrant's float joined on the name (cik_weak) and is disputed. TechCrunch 2014-05-22: 'the startup raised $1.6 million in seed funding last year from First Round, Freestyle, Google Ventures, Sherpa Ventures' and Steve Anderson, so the entry is the 2013 seed. TechCrunch 2016-07-27: $600k more went into LaunchKit and the team then joined Google, open-sourcing LaunchKit. Status departs from First Round's 'defunct': the Cluster app still runs in 2026, built and maintained by its makers under their own small company, Fotoloce ('We built Cluster', cluster.co/about read 2026-09-28), so the business operates and the acqui-hire decides nothing (s6). Flagged for review. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Live-services backend and SDK for game developers, relaunched in 2020 from the 'Boston-based' game studio Disruptor Beam (TechCrunch 2017-02-02, 2020-04-21), which went through a Subchapter V reorganization. Rounds read: $3.2M Series A (GrandBanks), a 2017 Series B led by GrandBanks and Romulus, and a $5M round in February 2021 led by Companyon Ventures and GrandBanks (GamesBeat); none names GV, which the firm's archive lists from 2020, so undetermined. Skillz acquired Beamable in January 2026 (Wikipedia).

Furnished mid-term rentals for business travellers (formerly HomeSuite, San Francisco). HomeSuite's $2.3M of 2015 came from Battery, Foundation and Bessemer (TechCrunch 2015-06-11, no GV). TechCrunch 2019-02-04: 2nd Address 'picks up $10M from GV, Foundation', GV leading, with $42M raised to date including debt-era money; the round is not named, so undetermined. Status aligned with Battery's row (acquired by Blueground in 2021); no sale document was read.

Valet storage and reusable moving boxes (AngelPad 2013, San Francisco). TechCrunch 2014-04-16: $2.3M from 'Floodgate Capital, Google Ventures, 500 Startups, Techstars, Jason Calacanis, and Ludlow Ventures'; the round is not named, so undetermined. Still operating: boxbee.com (read 2026-09-28) takes orders across the Bay Area and Southern California. No sale or later round found.

Bento Labs' context-aware Android home screen. TechCrunch 2015-03-11: '$2 million in seed funding from investors that include First Round Capital, Social+Capital, Google Ventures, Susa Ventures' and Silicon Valley angels. The Wikidata CA is a one-word join (another Bento) and is disputed: the company is a US startup on its investors' record, but no source read places its city. No source gives its fate after the 2015 beta, so status unknown. First Round's and YC's 'Bento' rows are other companies (Bento for Business; a 2020 YC company), though First Round was also in this seed. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Direct-to-consumer $3 essentials (San Francisco, product team in Minneapolis). TechCrunch 2017-07-11: seed from Cowboy and Slow, 'Redpoint led the company's Series A round, and NEA and GV just closed a $35 million Series B', so GV entered at the Series B: Growth. After SoftBank's $240M round (2018) it closed in February 2020 (Fortune headline, 2020-02-11). The brand was later relaunched by new owners (Clarke Capital Partners, per Wikipedia); aligned with Redpoint's defunct, the venture-backed company having ended, though the asset-sale reading of s6 would make it acquired: flagged.

Android casual games studio of Charles Hudson and Mike Jimenez. GamesBeat 2012-01-17: 'San Francisco-based Bionic Panda' raised seed financing, 'raised last year and ... announced for the first time today', from Google Ventures, SoftTech VC, Norwest, 500 Startups and angels. No source read gives the company's end, so status unknown. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

FX workflow and liquidity-access tools for institutional money managers. FX Week 2014-10-01: the 'Boston-based firm' closed before its planned July launch after a key deal with a global FX manager fell through, 'despite receiving $2 million from Google Ventures ... as well as investment from Atlas Venture, FreshTracks Capital and Boston Seed Capital' (CEO Ty Danco). The round is not named or dated, so undetermined; defunct.

Autonomous medical and retail drone delivery (Half Moon Bay in 2016, now South San Francisco). VentureBeat 2016-11-09 on the $25M Series B led by Visionnaire (with Sequoia and a16z): 'Google Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz ... are investors', total past $40M; the firm's own list carried Zipline in spring 2016, before that round, but no source read names the round GV bought, so undetermined. Mark: the $600M round of January 2026 at $7.6B (TechCrunch 2026-01-21), replacing the unicorn-list figure as the source; aligned with a16z, Felicis and Sequoia.

Security and governance platform for enterprise AI use and AI agents (Mountain View, per its site and the 2026 release; the 2024 release was datelined San Mateo). The company's release of 2024-05-21: a '$27.5 million Series A round, co-led by GV and Ballistic Ventures', Ballistic having incubated it since 2023; matches the firm's /ai list ('Invested' 2024-05). Sound Ventures led a $58M round on 2026-01-13 (Fin Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Ventures, Forgepoint; GV not named). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News, both releases): no valuation disclosed and no $1B+ priced round found, so below_1b.

Epigenetic editing therapeutics (Cambridge MA). The Series B release of 2023-03-01 (Sixth Street's copy): $135M, 'Financing led by GV', with ARCH, DCVC Bio, Mubadala and Sixth Street as new investors and an existing-investor list (Atlas, Newpath, Cormorant, Omega and others) that does not include GV, so GV entered at the Series B: Growth. The firm's own post (https://www.gv.com/news/chroma-medicine-dr-catherine-stehman-breen) names the same GV-led Series B. On 2024-12-11 Chroma and Nvelop Therapeutics combined as nChroma Bio, led by Nvelop's CEO Jeff Walsh, with $75M of new money; the two already shared ARCH, Atlas and GV as investors (BioPharma Dive). Read as acquired: the company folded into the combined nChroma Bio, which the firm lists as its own row (nchroma-bio), as it listed Nvelop (nvelop-therapeutics).

funding_rounds.round: Merger with Nvelop Therapeutics into nChroma Bio ($75M financing)
funding_rounds.lead: Cormorant, ARCH Venture Partners, Atlas Venture, Newpath Partners

note: Social marketplace built on Facebook ('a San Francisco startup', co-founded by Jim Rose). TechCrunch 2012-07-12: Foundation Capital led a $5M Series A 'with Google Ventures and Relay Ventures participating', all three having invested in the '$2 million seed funding round that closed in the spring of 2011', so the entry is that seed and the named Series A graduates it. Jim Rose's own account (interview, 2021): after the Facebook traffic fell the company pivoted to mobile tooling as 'Distiller', and 'In 2014, Distiller was acquired by CircleCI': acquired.

Construction labor marketplace matching trades workers to contractors (co-founded by Di-Ann Eisnor, ex-Waze). The company's release of 2020-09-21, datelined Palo Alto: $4M 'in its seed funding round from investors including Pete Flint (NFX), John Lyman (Google Ventures)', Rob Hayes and Caterina Fake; John Lyman is the GV partner on the firm's listing. bycore.com now forwards to a parked page and no source read gives the company's later state, so status unknown. YC's 'Core' (Bangalore, S23) is a different company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Cinch Polls, the social photo-polling app spun out of the price-tracker Nifti (Nathan Sharp). Nifti's $1.2M additional seed of December 2013 came from Otto Capital and angels, without GV (TechCrunch 2014-09-25); the company's March 2015 release, datelined Boston, cites 'backing from a group of investors including Google Ventures'. No source read names or dates GV's round, so undetermined; no source gives the company's later state, so status unknown.
